feedback: Revise before racing. The sensor span change is a sound single-variable test, but the weights are not. The candidate sets the outer sensors to ±1.5, so the steering signal can reach ±1.5 where iteration 3 (best raced, 361.4) reached ±1.0. That raises the effective proportional gain by about 1.5x (kp 2.5 behaves like about 3.75 at the edge). Iteration 2 showed that a higher effective gain with a larger footprint cut oval finishes (0.55) and raised steering_oscillation (0.27), so this change could cause the same oval damage. It would also confound the span test, which the team has already had trouble reading. Keep the signal scale equal to iteration 3 by spreading the seven weights across the same ±1.0 range, for example [-1.0, -0.67, -0.33, 0.0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0]. The rest of the candidate (7 sensors at x = ±0.075, 0.025 m spacing, y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012, kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.1, last_direction) can stay as it is. The 0.025 m spacing with 12 mm footprints still covers the 25 mm tape, so there is no gap for the line to hide in. Once the revision is in, race it with the scale matched; the race will show whether the outer coverage fixes line loss on the s-bend and slalom. Do not infer its performance from the rationale, which is a hypothesis.
requested_changes: Set sensor_weights to a scale-matched spread across the same ±1.0 range, for example [-1.0, -0.67, -0.33, 0.0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0], so the signal peak matches iteration 3 (kp 2.5 unchanged). This keeps the span as the only effective change, since iteration 2 showed that a higher effective gain hurts the oval.

Keep the 7 sensors at x = -0.075, -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.075 m, y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012, kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.1, last_direction. Iteration 3 (same gains, 5 sensors at ±0.06) finished the oval 20 of 20, so this isolates the span effect.

If the scale-matched race still ends slalom and s-bend off track with line_loss_events near 1 and max_error at or above 0.06 m, the limit is turn authority rather than coverage. Then raise kp from 2.5 to about 3.0 on the same scale-matched weights, not on the 1.5-scaled weights.
